Name: Sanguinous Rain
Description:
A swirling crimson cloud appears above you, centered on a point you can see within the spell’s range. This cloud has a radius of 60 feet, and must appear from a point at least 60 feet above you (otherwise the spell fails). A drizzle of blood-like rain begins to fall from this cloud, dousing any exposed flames (including magical flames of a level below this spell’s). The cloud remains for the spell’s duration.

Once when you cast the spell, then again as an action on subsequent turns, you can choose one creature who is under the cloud to make a Constitution saving throw, as the blood attempts to seep into their skin and poison them. On a failure, they take 3d10 poison damage and are poisoned until the end of your next turn.

As an action, you may also choose to end this spell early and cause a sudden downpour of blood. If you do, you can target any number of creatures under the cloud to make the Constitution save described above, with the same consequences, then the spell ends.
At Higher Levels:
When you cast this spell at 3rd level or higher, you can choose one of the following effects for each level above 2nd:
● The spell’s damage increases by 1d10.
● When you select a target to make the Constitution saving throw, you can choose one additional target in the rain.
● (2 slot levels) The radius of the cloud doubles.
